When questioned regarding his riding in the early stages of the Home Straight and the vigour he applied to the horse, L Ferraris stated that after following GOLD TACK his intention was to improve between GOLD TACK and CARRYON SMILING as HAILTOTHEVICTORS had raced best when improving between runners. He said after receiving this crowding HAILTOTHEVICTORS then finished the race off well.

Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that with the early and middle stages being run inside of standard time she was obliged to make use of her mount to hold a forward position which resulted in CARRYON SMILING giving ground in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race which included an endoscopic examination showed a substantial amount of blood in the horse’s trachea.  Before being allowed to race again, CARRYON SMILING will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

When questioned K Teetan stated that his instructions were to take up a forward position and he was given the option to lead if circumstances permitted.  He said after jumping well from a wide barrier he allowed his mount to stride forward where he was positioned to the outside of CARRYON SMILING near the 1200 Metres.  He said when HAPPY BUDDIES improved marginally in front of CARRYON SMILING he then elected to allow HAPPY BUDDIES to continue forward to cross that runner near the 900 Metres.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to remain racing to the outside of CARRYON SMILING, having regard to the early stages being run inside of standard time, K Teetan stated that as his mount was travelling comfortably and he did not have to make use of the horse to cross CARRYON SMILING, he felt this was the best option to give the horse the chance to finish in the best possible placing.  After considering his explanation and taking into account the sectional times the Stewards advised Jockey Teetan that, in their opinion, he would have been better suited by remaining to the outside of CARRYON SMILING in the early stages which would have set a more sustainable pace throughout the early and middle stages of the event.
